title: Measuring Strain in Moirés from Overlapping Dark Field Reflections in 4D-STEM
content: Moiré materials, containing structural beating patterns from vertically aligning thin layers with a small rotational and/or lattice offset, are a powerful physical simulator of correlated electron physics and show promise as ferroelectric, optoelectronic, and catalytic materials. Central to these pursuits are techniques to thoroughly characterize the structure of moiré superlattices, as spontaneous structural relaxation substantially influences their physical properties. One route to measuring moiré-level strain in (possibly encapsulated) moiré materials involves fitting the intensity of overlapping Bragg disks to simple trigonometric expressions in a 4D-STEM acquisition [1-4].
